shortAnswer: You should not assume you are starting over. Ask these universities to evaluate the original transcript against a current business degree before replacing any old courses. Older general education and eligible business coursework may still help, but subject-specific currency, grades, current degree requirements and residency decide the result.
sourceCreditVsReceivingAward: An earned course remains part of the original academic record. Whether and where a receiving school awards credit is a separate current decision; an old catalog or unfinished degree plan is not a permanent promise of current degree applicability.

schoolPolicies.scope: Business bachelor's area of study; verify the selected BS/BSBA program's current structure.
schoolPolicies.generalAgeDisposition: No blanket expiry for all college credit established. Current transfer policy explicitly says some programs have age rules for area-of-study courses.
schoolPolicies.businessCurrency: At most 50 percent of area-of-study courses may be older than 10 years from the most current application date. The remaining area-of-study credits must be within 10 years. Business capstone credit must be no more than five years old; older capstone must be retaken.
schoolPolicies.grade: Transfer policy requires at least C for composition and area of study. The chosen program may impose additional business-core rules.
schoolPolicies.residency: Standard nonmilitary per-credit/full-time routes require 15 eligible TESU AC/OL/NU/GS/EP credits; an Edison Accelerate fee can waive that residency. Transfer policy separately requires SOS-1100 and the capstone at TESU.
schoolPolicies.catalogCurrency: A lapse greater than three years or a degree change moves the student to the catalog effective at re-enrollment/change. This concerns graduation requirements, not erasing source credits.
schoolPolicies.specificStudentImplication: Twenty-five-year-old general education should be evaluated separately from any business concentration courses; do not reject the whole transcript or promise all old major work.

schoolPolicies.scope: BS Business Management, Catalog 05-2026, general transfer guidelines.
schoolPolicies.generalAgeDisposition: The current guideline has course-specific limits, rather than a stated blanket five-year age limit on all college courses.
schoolPolicies.businessCurrency: D388 Fundamentals of Spreadsheets and Data Presentations requires coursework within five years. C722 Project Management requires the course/certification within five years of the start date. Certain HR certifications require completion/renewal within five years. The partner guide separately names five-year limits for IT-specific courses and certifications.
schoolPolicies.grade: General threshold C−; business courses require C or better.
schoolPolicies.residency: At least 25 percent of required degree competency units, excluding capstone, at WGU under the guideline wording; nontransferable courses also remain.
schoolPolicies.catalogCurrency: Evaluation is specific to current degree pathway; a change of degree requires reevaluation. WGU must receive official transcripts before first term; do not start and expect later transfer credit.
schoolPolicies.specificStudentImplication: An old writing, history or eligible business course can still be considered; old spreadsheets/project management need particular review. Two years without an awarded degree cannot be treated as satisfied-by-degree.

schoolPolicies.scope: Undergraduate online transfer policy and undergraduate registrar course exceptions, separate from graduate business rules.
schoolPolicies.generalAgeDisposition: Catalog states lifetime credit acceptance except courses whose content faculty determine changes significantly over time.
schoolPolicies.businessCurrency: Undergraduate registrar sets a five-year limit for all upper-level ACCT courses and all CSIS/CSCN courses. Selected DIGI courses have ten-year limits. The business registrar page's graduate ten-year/doctoral seven-year rules do not apply wholesale to this bachelor's scenario.
schoolPolicies.grade: Undergraduate registrar lists C or higher; catalog and registrar pass-grade language has qualifications that should be checked against the original transcript.
schoolPolicies.residency: At least 25 percent of total degree and 25 percent of major through Liberty.
schoolPolicies.catalogCurrency: Use the current chosen degree completion plan and exact equivalency dates; accepted elective credit might not fill a remaining degree slot. Foreign capstones do not replace Liberty capstones.
schoolPolicies.specificStudentImplication: Lower-division old general education and business deserve evaluation; do not generalize upper-level accounting or graduate rules to all credits.

schoolPolicies.school: University of Maine at Presque Isle
schoolPolicies.scope: YourPace BA Business Administration, current university transfer policy and FAQ.
schoolPolicies.generalAgeDisposition: No explicit current blanket age exclusion or no-expiry promise verified; formal receiving review remains necessary.
schoolPolicies.businessCurrency: No current business-specific accounting/IT age cutoff established in bounded research. Archived readmission clauses are not applied to this new external-transfer scenario.
schoolPolicies.grade: C− or higher from an accepted accredited institution; P/S/CR must mean at least C−.
schoolPolicies.residency: Current FAQ: at least 30 UMPI credits, including 12 major credits, at least 9 of those at 300 level or above.
schoolPolicies.catalogCurrency: Receiving academic unit determines applicability to current degree/program requirements. An archive readmission condition is not silently imported into current external transfer policy.
schoolPolicies.specificStudentImplication: Request an actual evaluation of old general education and business courses. Do not replace them simply because they are old, or promise all will count.

schoolPolicies.scope: MyPath self-paced BBA; distinguish MyPath B− standard from general transfer-grade policies.
schoolPolicies.generalAgeDisposition: Official March 9, 2026 application guide explicitly says undergraduate transfer credits have no time limit.
schoolPolicies.businessCurrency: No separate current undergraduate BBA accounting/IT expiry established. Credits still need current course and competency equivalence and program applicability.
schoolPolicies.grade: B− or better from institutionally accredited institutions for MyPath.
schoolPolicies.residency: Current MyPath BBA requires 120 credits and advertises at most 90 transferable credits. The official indexed 2025–2026 competency-based catalog states 30 equivalent credits in residence including LBSC 320/321; keep this catalog year visible and confirm any later requirement change.
schoolPolicies.catalogCurrency: Use a current program evaluation; no claim that a 25-year-old degree plan remains binding.
schoolPolicies.freshStartException: Academic Fresh Start is elective at admission/readmission. It excludes all coursework 10 or more years old; excluded courses receive no credit and cannot satisfy prerequisites or degree requirements. Do not recommend it casually to a student hoping to reuse those credits.
schoolPolicies.specificStudentImplication: Potentially useful age policy if old grades are at least B− and the courses fill current MyPath competencies. A C-level old course may produce a different comparison with UMPI/TESU/Liberty.

article.finding: Existing article correctly rejects a blanket expiry assumption, highlights course-specific WGU rules, preserves source credits and distinguishes approximate prior credits from applied degree credit.
article.usefulImprovement: Update the existing old-credit article with a short five-school business comparison, explicit TESU/WGU/Liberty exceptions, MyPath B− and Fresh Start boundary, UMPI retrieval uncertainty, and the difference between original credits and a current catalog. No new duplicate article needed.

importer.dateBehavior: Exact dates retained; a printed year or term is preserved in original source metadata while completedOn stays blank. No date or credit quantity is guessed.
importer.acceptanceBehavior: Importing original learning is not a receiving-school transfer award.

recencyEngine.finding: Source-bound course-specific recency rules use completedOn and preserve the original record; missing required dates cause review. Generic course-age comparison currently uses today's UTC date rather than a user-entered future start date.
recencyEngine.limitation: A student-facing estimate must not present the current-date recency check as an official start-date evaluation.

tesuGroupedCurrency.finding: Application-date currency review is currently hard-scoped to TESU Accounting and Finance. It requests an individual review, rather than guessing the most recent application date.
tesuGroupedCurrency.potentialGap: Review separately whether other TESU business models need source-bound currency groups. Do not reuse the 18-credit/9-older-credit structure blindly in another program.

nextSteps: Request the original official transcript and retain an unofficial copy for planning.
Record every actually earned course, grade, source credit unit and completion date; do not assume two years equals 60 semester credits.
Compare current business degree evaluations from a small shortlist before buying replacement general education.
Separate rejected age-limited major/prerequisite work from still-useful general education or electives.
Choose new courses only for remaining requirements after grade, recency and residency review.
At UMass Global, compare normal transfer evaluation before considering the optional Academic Fresh Start forfeiture.

UMPI/UMass Global direct catalog pages reported tool 403; official university transfer/program pages were read directly. UMass residency catalog indexed text is specifically 2025–2026. UMPI current no-expiry statement was not established.
